key: And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed; and she had not known man.
s: Jephthah’s only daughter, first out to meet him after his vow of a burnt-offering, comes home from the mountains; Rashi, on 11:39, takes her as lost because neither Jephthah nor Phinehas, who could release the vow, would stoop to go to the other, and Radak, on 11:39, as set apart in a house, away from people.

evidence.words: ותהי חק. גזרו שלא יעשה אדם עוד כן, שאלו הלך אצל פנחס, או הוא בא אצלו, היה מתיר לו נדרו, עמדו בגדולתן, ומבין שניהם אבדה … ויעש לה את נדרו אשר נדר. שעשה לה בית והכניסה שם והיתה שם פרושה מבני אדם ומדרכי העולם
evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 11:39, ‘and it was a custom’:] They decreed that no one should do so again, for had he gone to Phinehas, or had Phinehas come to him, he would have released his vow; they stood on their greatness, and between the two of them she was lost … [Radak on 11:39, ‘and he did with her his vow which he had vowed’:] that he made her a house and brought her into it, and there she was set apart from people and from the ways of the world.

reason: verse.js ok, ref Judges 11:39 and at [221,39] match. Plain sense faithful: the daughter is his only child who meets him (11:34) after his vow to offer a burnt-offering (11:31) and returns after two months on the mountains (11:37 to 38); no four-word run from the key verse. Read the chapter 11 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on Judges). Rashi on ותהי חק (within 11:39 in JPS) says Phinehas could have released the vow had either gone to the other, but they stood on their greatness and between them she was lost: the sentence stays within it. Radak on ויעש לה את נדרו at 11:39 says he made her a house where she was set apart from people and the ways of the world (he gives the same view at 11:31 in his father’s name and reports the rabbinic Phinehas story at 11:40 as a mistaken vow); the sentence names the two readings without resolving them. Both evidence pieces machine-found in the packet. entry-check ok. Sensitivity flagged as violence (a vow of a burnt-offering fulfilled on a daughter), though the lane is non-sensitive; the plain clause states the vow plainly.
